question.problem: A triangle has sides $j$, $k$, and $l.$ The sides $j$ and $l$ have lengths $4$ and $7$, respectively. If the angle $K$ between $j$ and $l$ has a measure of ${121}^{∘}$, what is the length of side $k?$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252321/assets/1fde3029f6a50388ebd342dc4d15e9787567461b651c24cd6bd6843521b0465d.png)

The Law of Cosines states that

$$
{k}^{2}={j}^{2}+{l}^{2}-2jl\operatorname{cos}⁡K.
$$

Here, we have

$$
m∠K={121}^{∘},\,j=4,\,l=7.
$$

Substituting the numbers into the formula gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{k}^{2} & ={4}^{2}+{7}^{2}-2(4)(7)\operatorname{cos}⁡{121}^{∘} \\  & =16+49-56\operatorname{cos}⁡{121}^{∘} \\  & =65-56(-0.515\,03…) \\  & =65+28.842\,13 \\  & =93.842\,13\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $5$ decimal places. 

Taking the square root gives

$$
k=\sqrt{93.842\,13}=9.69
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
